necessary.title: Necessary
necessary.description: States a needed capability or constraint; removing it leaves the product incomplete. If nothing breaks without it, it is superfluous.

implementation_free.title: Implementation-free
implementation_free.description: Says what, not how: does not impose architecture, technology, storage format or protocol without a real need.

unambiguous.title: Unambiguous
unambiguous.description: Can be read only one way: no vague words, undefined terms, unspecified units, time zones or interval bounds.

complete.title: Complete
complete.description: Needs no guessing: conditions, error handling and edge cases are described; no “to be defined later”.

singular.title: Singular
singular.description: One requirement — one capability or constraint; no “and/or” bundling several behaviours.

feasible.title: Feasible
feasible.description: Achievable within reasonable technical, time and budget constraints.

verifiable.title: Verifiable
verifiable.description: A finite objective way (test, analysis, inspection) exists to prove it; measurable criteria are given.

correct.title: Correct
correct.description: Accurately reflects the stakeholder need and the domain; contains no factual errors.

conforming.title: Conforming
conforming.description: Follows the agreed template and style of the document.

traceable.title: Traceable
traceable.description: Has an identifier and a clear source; tests and child documents can refer to it.

set_complete.title: Complete (set)
set_complete.description: The set covers all needed capabilities, errors, states and interfaces; template sections are filled in.

set_consistent.title: Consistent
set_consistent.description: Requirements do not contradict each other, acceptance criteria or child documents; terms and units are used uniformly.

set_feasible.title: Feasible (set)
set_feasible.description: The set as a whole is achievable within project constraints.

set_comprehensible.title: Comprehensible
set_comprehensible.description: It is clear what the system is expected to do and how it relates to its environment.

set_validatable.title: Able to be validated
set_validatable.description: It can be shown that meeting the set satisfies the business need.

set_ranked.title: Ranked
set_ranked.description: Importance and/or stability is stated for requirements.

set_modifiable.title: Modifiable
set_modifiable.description: The structure allows changes without duplication; the document is versioned.

set_traceable.title: Traceable (set)
set_traceable.description: Links between requirements, acceptance criteria and child documents can be followed.

auth.title: The provider rejected the API key
auth.hint: Check the key in Settings: it may be truncated, revoked or issued for another project.

forbidden.title: No access to the model
forbidden.hint: The key works, but the account has no access to this model or region. Pick another model or enable access in the provider console.

rate_limit.title: Too many requests (provider limit)
rate_limit.hint: Free tiers limit requests per minute. Increase the pause between calls (5–10 s), set concurrency to 1 and run again.

quota.title: Quota exhausted or billing missing
quota.hint: The daily limit or account balance has run out. Top up, wait for the quota reset or switch provider.

not_found.title: Model not found at the provider
not_found.hint: Pick a model from the list in Settings. If the list is empty, check the key or server address.

bad_request.title: The provider rejected the request
bad_request.hint: Usually a parameter the selected model does not support. Try another model; if it persists, pass the details to an administrator.

context.title: The document does not fit the model context
context.hint: Reduce the batch size in AI parameters or pick a model with a larger context.

timeout.title: The model did not answer in time
timeout.hint: Local and reasoning models are slow. Increase the run timeout in AI parameters or reduce the batch size.

connection.title: Cannot reach the provider
connection.hint: The model server is unreachable from ReqCheck. Check the base URL, the server and the proxy.

unavailable.title: The provider is temporarily unavailable
unavailable.hint: The provider is overloaded or failing. Wait a couple of minutes and run again; you can also raise the number of attempts.

invalid_output.title: The model returned malformed output
invalid_output.hint: Weaker models sometimes break JSON. Reduce the batch size, raise the attempts or pick a stronger model.

not_configured.title: The provider is not configured
not_configured.hint: Set a key (for a local model — the server address) in Settings.

not_implemented.title: This agent feature is not ready yet
not_implemented.hint: This part of the core is not implemented on the server yet. Tell an administrator.

cancelled.title: Run cancelled
cancelled.hint: The run was stopped by a user or by timeout. You can run it again.

unknown.title: Error while calling the model
unknown.hint: See the details below. If it persists, pass them to an administrator.

modelNotFound.title: Model “{{model}}” not found at the provider
modelNotFound.hint: The key works, but the provider has no such model (or the account cannot use it). Pick a model from the “Default model” list and save.

params.defaultsHint: Used for new runs and chat when nothing else is chosen.
params.pacingHint: Tune to the provider plan: free keys are rate-limited, local models are slow.

preset.free_geminiHint: 6 s pause, 1 worker, 8 attempts — to stay clear of 429
preset.paid_apiHint: No pause, 4 workers, batches of 8 — fast
preset.localHint: 1 worker, batches of 3, 4 attempts, 1 h run timeout — for a single GPU

min_interval_s.label: Pause between calls
min_interval_s.hint: Free Gemini and 429 “Too many requests” errors — set 5–10 s. Paid plans and local models — 0.

concurrency.label: Parallel requests
concurrency.hint: Paid APIs — 3–4, runs get several times faster. Free keys and a local model on one GPU — 1, otherwise 429 or queueing.

max_attempts.label: Attempts per call
max_attempts.hint: Retries on 429, 5xx and network drops. 4–6 is usually enough; 8 on free tiers. More means longer hangs on real failures.

batch_size.label: Requirements per request
batch_size.hint: Bigger — fewer and cheaper calls, but weak models break JSON more often. On format or context errors drop to 3–4.

run_timeout_s.label: Whole run timeout
run_timeout_s.hint: Runs longer than this stop with an error. Local and reasoning models, large documents — 3600 s or more (up to 6 h).

params.embeddingsHint: The model that turns text into vectors for semantic search over runs and the knowledge base.

emb.localHint: Works offline, data never leaves. Recommended for a bank perimeter.
emb.geminiHint: Better on long texts, but texts are sent to Google.
emb.openaiHint: Paid, texts are sent to OpenAI.

params.reindexWarning: After changing the embeddings model the knowledge base and run history are re-indexed — search may be incomplete for a few minutes.

max_upload_mb.label: Upload size limit
max_upload_mb.hint: Maximum size of a document or knowledge-base file. Scanned PDFs can be heavy — 50–100 MB.

session_ttl_hours.label: Session lifetime
session_ttl_hours.hint: Hours until the user has to sign in again. For a shared computer — 1–2 h.

params.embDimHint: Gemini only. 768 balances quality and index size.
params.embModelBuiltin: Default: the embeddings service built-in model

runView.sceneLabel: Agent conveyor: the document passes seven agents on its way to the report
runView.stackLabel: Layer stack: each agent is a layer

parsing.role: Reads PDF, DOCX, MD and TXT, normalises the text and keeps offsets that quotes are later checked against.

segmenting.role: Extracts requirements and acceptance criteria: an LLM plus hints from IDs, acceptance lines and API response codes. Splits compound ones into sub-requirements.

rule_checks.role: Rules without an LLM: vague words in Russian and English, TBD markers, empty template fields, document version.

checking_requirements.role: Checks every requirement against the 10 criteria of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 5.2.5 and IEEE 830 4.3, in batches, with knowledge base snippets.

checking_set.role: Six reviewers with different roles look at the whole set: two consistency controllers (rule logic and spec consistency), a systems analyst, a QA analyst, an integration architect, and a risk and security analyst.

verifying.role: Checks quotes against the text by code, then the verifier tries to refute every finding, aligns severity and merges duplicates in two passes.

rendering.role: Prepares clarifying questions for the author and writes the conclusion: can development and testing start, what to fix first. Builds MD, DOCX, PDF and JSON exports.
